title: wave start: no way to skip the spec check the owner declined

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Observed 2026-11-11 (slicer wave): the owner chose no spec check at Setup (the relay contract makes it optional), but `ork wave start` started a spec-check step (claude sonnet) on its own; `ork --help` lists no flag to turn it off for one wave (only `ork projects set --spec-check-rows`, which picks rows). Wanted: a per-start flag such as --spec-check off.

Re-anchored 2026-11-18:

- The contract says the spec check is optional and that Setup asks the owner whether to run one (`slicer ai relay`, Roles and Setup). ork runs it on every start: `startWave` calls `a.specCheck` with no way around it (`internal/cli/wave.go:381-382`), and so does `ork run` (`internal/cli/run.go:119`, `internal/cli/run.go:143`). The TUI Waves launch starts it too (`confirmWave` -> `startSpecCheck`, `internal/tui/waves.go:305-313`).
- adj 164 (`roles.spec-check`, decided 2026-10-25) chose a batch spec check before a wave; it does not say whether the owner may skip it for one start.
- The daemon does not need a spec check to start a run: `specGate` passes an item with no remembered check (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:695-701`). It still refuses an item whose last check left open questions on the same spec (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:711-721`), so a skip cannot jump past unanswered questions.
- What a skip loses: the answers' decisions paragraph a run carries (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1188`); a local implementer's orientation pack, and a run without one starts without it (adj 361, `speccheck.cached-verdict-no-pack`); the carve of a local slice above size S, which the daemon already refuses without its slivers (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1060-1065`).
- No open ork item covers it (`slicer find "spec check"` and the open list, 2026-11-18). S337 (no terminal) is separate: it stops a spec check that cannot lead to a start.

Open owner question: where the skip lives (CLI flag only, TUI too, or a project setting), per the owner's answer to `cli.spec-check-skip`.

This slice touches `internal/cli` output (and the TUI if the owner picks it), so it gets a UI pass (rule u10).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/wave.go:240-424` (`waveOptions`, `waveStart`, `startWave`: the flag and the skip)
- `internal/cli/run.go:100-170` (`ork run`: the same flag)
- `internal/cli/wave_test.go`
- `internal/cli/run_test.go`
- `internal/cli/cli.go` (usage text for both commands)
- `docs/guide.md`
- `docs/design.md` (spec check section: the owner may skip it, citing the new record)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Written for the recommended answer to `cli.spec-check-skip` (a `--spec-check off` flag on `ork run` and `ork wave start`). Adjust to the owner's answer.

- `TestWaveStartSpecCheckOffSkipsTheCheck` in `internal/cli/wave_test.go`: `ork wave start p S1 S2 --spec-check off --yes` with a `specStub`. Expect no `spec.check` call, one `wave.start` call with both items, and the line `spec check: off (--spec-check off)` before the start. Red today: the flag is unknown, so the command is a usage error.
- `TestRunSpecCheckOffSkipsTheCheck` in `internal/cli/run_test.go`: the same for `ork run p S1 --spec-check off --yes`. Red today: unknown flag.
- `TestSpecCheckFlagTakesOnlyOff` in `internal/cli/wave_test.go`: `--spec-check on` and `--spec-check maybe` are usage errors that name `off`. Red today: unknown flag.
- `TestSpecCheckOffWithQuestionsOrAnswerIsAUsageError` in `internal/cli/wave_test.go`: `--spec-check off` with `--questions` or `--answer` is a usage error, since both need the check. Red today: unknown flag.
- `TestSpecCheckOffStillRefusesOpenQuestions` in `internal/cli/wave_test.go`: a stub whose `wave.start` replies `spec_questions` for S1 ("S1 has 2 open spec questions; answer them first"); with `--spec-check off --yes` the CLI prints that refusal and exits non-zero. Red today: unknown flag.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and see each red for the stated reason.
2. Per the owner's answer to `cli.spec-check-skip`: add `--spec-check off` to `ork wave start` and `ork run` (a string flag; only `off` is valid; with `--questions` or `--answer` it is a usage error).
3. With the flag, `startWave` and `ork run` skip `a.specCheck`, print `spec check: off (--spec-check off)` to the prompts writer, keep every planned item, and go on to the confirm. The daemon's `specGate` refusal stays as it is.
4. If the owner's answer includes the TUI or a project setting, add those in this slice per that answer; otherwise the TUI keeps running the check.
5. Usage text in `internal/cli/cli.go` for both commands.
6. Docs: `docs/guide.md` (the flag and what a skip loses: answers' decisions, a local orientation pack, a local carve), `docs/design.md` spec check section citing the new record. Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S338 --text "..."`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- ork wave start and ork run with --spec-check off run no spec check, say so in one line, and start the planned items after the usual confirm.
- Without the flag, both commands behave as before.
- --spec-check takes only off, and is refused with --questions or --answer.
- An item whose last spec check left open questions is still refused by the daemon.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/cli -run 'SpecCheckOff|SpecCheckFlagTakesOnlyOff' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- `adj lint` exits 0.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, message "S338: --spec-check off skips the spec check for one start".
